_note: Criteria trees transcribed ONLY from the manual text (section numbers given per leaf). Built before any criteria-tree run. Operators: AND = every child must hold; OR = at least one child holds. Liability, notice, waiver, reopening and other procedural issues are NOT coverage criteria in these manual sections and are out of scope for the tree.

children.text: Prior hospitalization and transfer requirements are met (ch.8 s20)

The beneficiary was a hospital INPATIENT for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days (day of admission counts, day of discharge does not; time in observation or the emergency room does not count).
The beneficiary was transferred to a participating SNF within 30 days after hospital discharge (or the s20.2 exception applies).
The four SNF level-of-care factors are all met (ch.8 s30)
The patient requires skilled nursing or skilled rehabilitation services ordered by a physician, for a condition treated in the hospital or arising in the SNF
The patient needs direct skilled nursing services (services so inherently complex they can be safely and effectively performed only by or under the supervision of a registered nurse).
The patient needs direct skilled therapy services (physical therapy, speech-language pathology or occupational therapy requiring the skills of a therapist).
The patient needs skilled management and evaluation of a care plan (the total care, skilled or not, must be planned and managed by skilled nursing personnel).

The patient needs skilled observation and assessment because there is a likelihood of change in condition requiring skilled personnel to evaluate need for modified treatment, until the condition is essentially stabilized.
The patient needs skilled teaching and training activities requiring skilled personnel to teach the patient to manage the treatment regimen.
The patient requires the skilled services on a DAILY basis (skilled nursing or rehabilitation seven days a week, or skilled rehabilitation at least five days a week).
As a practical matter, considering economy and efficiency, the daily skilled services can be provided only on an inpatient basis in a SNF.

The services delivered are reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the illness or injury: consistent with its nature and severity, the individual's particular medical needs and accepted standards of medical practice, and reasonable in duration and quantity.

root.text: Medicare covers these home health services

children.text: The patient is confined to the home (ch.7 s30.1.1)
Criterion One
Because of illness or injury, the patient needs supportive devices (crutches, canes, wheelchair, walker), special transportation, or the assistance of another person in order to leave the residence.
The patient has a condition such that leaving home is medically contraindicated.
There exists a normal inability to leave home.
Leaving home requires a considerable and taxing effort.
The patient is under the care of a physician or allowed practitioner.
The services are furnished under a plan of care established and periodically reviewed by a physician or allowed practitioner.
The patient needs a qualifying skilled service

The patient needs skilled nursing care on an intermittent basis (fewer than 7 days each week or less than 8 hours each day for 21 days or less) that is reasonable and necessary, such as skilled observation and assessment, management and evaluation of a care plan, or teaching.
The patient needs physical therapy or speech-language pathology that is reasonable and necessary, or has a continuing need for occupational therapy.

root.text: Inpatient rehabilitation facility care was reasonable and necessary and covered

children.text: The IRF medical record contains the required documentation: a pre-admission screening, an overall plan of care, and admission orders (s110.1).
The patient required the active and ongoing therapeutic intervention of multiple therapy disciplines (PT, OT, speech-language pathology, or prosthetics/orthotics), one of which must be PT or OT.
The patient generally required an intensive rehabilitation therapy program (generally at least 3 hours per day at least 5 days per week, or at least 15 hours per week).

The patient could reasonably be expected to actively participate in, and benefit significantly from, the intensive program, i.e., make measurable improvement of practical value within a prescribed period of time.
The patient required physician supervision by a rehabilitation physician, with face-to-face visits at least 3 days per week.
The patient required an intensive and coordinated interdisciplinary approach to providing rehabilitation.
